questions.q: Why does calling a Solidity `view` function cost no gas?
options: It never changes state, so the call is a read-only eth_call rather than a transaction
Gas fees were removed for all function calls in a recent Ethereum upgrade
View functions run on a separate, free sidechain
It only costs gas the first time any user calls it
questions.explain: A view (or pure) function is guaranteed not to modify state, so a node can just compute and return the result without a mined transaction — that's an eth_call, not a state-changing write.

questions.q: In ethers.js v6, what two things does `new ethers.Contract(...)` need to let you call a read function?
options: The contract's address and its ABI
The contract's bytecode and its compiler version
The user's private key and a gas limit
The block number and a transaction hash
questions.explain: A Contract instance is built from the deployed address plus the ABI describing its functions; the provider supplies the connection.

questions.q: In viem, which function do you call to read a native ETH balance?
options: client.getBalance({ address })
client.readContract({ functionName: "balance" })
client.sendTransaction({ value: 0 })
client.watchBlocks()
questions.explain: viem's public client exposes getBalance for native currency; readContract is for calling a contract's own functions like balanceOf on a token.

questions.q: What does Etherscan's Read Contract tab demonstrate that maps directly to code?
options: Calling a view function needs no wallet connection and no gas — exactly like an eth_call in your own code
Every contract function always requires a connected wallet to even view its name
Reading data from a contract always requires sending ETH first
Etherscan replaces the need for a node provider entirely
questions.explain: The Read Contract tab lets a human trigger free eth_call requests with no wallet — the same underlying call your code makes with provider/contract reads.

questions.q: A confirmed transaction's receipt — Status, Block, From, To, Value, Transaction Fee — is fetched in code with which kind of call?
options: A read call, such as getTransactionReceipt()
A write call that must be signed by the original sender
A call that requires deploying a new contract
A call only available through a paid Etherscan API plan
questions.explain: Once a transaction is mined, its receipt is public chain data — any provider/client can fetch it with a read-only call, no signature needed.
